cards.text: Pharaoh's men just sent Abram out of Egypt with his wife and everything he owns (Gen 12:20). So Abram goes up into the Negev, and his nephew Lot is with him (Gen 12:5). Friend, getting walked out the door by Pharaoh's men isn't a send-off, that's a BOUNCER.

cards.question: Abram leaves Egypt a whole lot richer than he showed up. What has he become extremely wealthy in?

cards.text: From the Negev, Abram travels from place to place toward Bethel. He ends up right back between Bethel and Ai, at the same spot where his tent was pitched before.

cards.question: Between Bethel and Ai, Abram comes back to the site where he had built the ___.
Back at that altar, Abram calls on the name of the LORD.

cards.text: Now Lot's not traveling light either. He's got flocks and herds and tents of his own, and friend, with that many animals in one place, I can already HEAR the trouble coming.

cards.question: Abram and Lot have so many possessions that the land can't support both of them while they stay together.
With the land stretched thin, discord breaks out. Who's fighting?

cards.text: And it's not just Abram and Lot out there. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites are living in the land too.
So Abram says to Lot, "Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen."

cards.question: Abram's reason for keeping the peace with Lot: after all, they are ___.

cards.text: Then Abram makes Lot an offer: "Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me." Friend, that's handing somebody the TV remote AND the good seat on the couch.

cards.question: Abram wants him and Lot to separate. If Lot goes to the left, what will Abram do?

cards.text: Lot looks out over the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar. It's like scrolling house listings and stopping DEAD on the one that makes you say WOW.

cards.question: What does Lot see when he looks out over the plain of the Jordan?
The plain is well watered like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt. Which land does Lot choose for himself?

answers.text: The whole plain of the Jordan

cards.text: Lot sets out toward the east, and just like that, Abram and Lot part company. Abram lives in the land of Canaan, and Lot settles in the cities of the plain.

cards.question: In the cities of the plain, Lot pitches his tent toward ___.
When Lot looks out over that plain, the LORD has already destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.

cards.text: Lot's got the greenest view around, but here's the catch about the neighbors. The men of Sodom were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.
After Lot has gone, the LORD speaks to Abram. He tells Abram to lift up his eyes and look north and south and east and west.

cards.question: Abram is looking in every direction. What does the LORD say about all the land he sees?

answers.text: He will give it to Abram and his offspring forever
Abram must share it with Lot and his family
Abram's offspring must win it in battle someday

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll make Abram's offspring like the dust of the earth, too many to count. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer counting dust as it fell, and I never got anywhere close to finishing.

cards.question: The LORD tells Abram to get up and ___ around the land, through its length and breadth, because He will give it to him.

cards.text: So Abram moves his tent and goes to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron. Lot walked off with the view, but Abram walked off with the PROMISE, and friend, I know which one I'm packing.

cards.question: At his new home near Hebron, Abram builds an altar to the LORD.

cards.text: Abram's settled in under those oaks for now, friend. But this family? They've got a LOT more coming.

findings.problem: "I can already HEAR the trouble coming" tells the baker something goes wrong before card 7 asks whether the land can support them both and card 8 asks about the discord. The setup line points straight to True.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question asks "Who's fighting?" but Genesis 13:7 says there was discord between the herdsmen. "Fighting" stretches "discord".

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The joke about stopping DEAD on the listing that makes you say WOW tells the baker the plain looks inviting. That rules out "It's dry and rocky" before card 2 asks what Lot sees.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word in the LORD's line (walk vs ride). Nothing earlier lets a baker reason it out, so the pick comes down to luck about the wording.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This choice card asks about the parenthetical in Genesis 13:10 after cards 4 and 5 have already moved on to Genesis 13:11-12, so the walkthrough steps back in the passage. The docs require stops to run in order, but they don't say whether a card inside a stop may return to an earlier verse.
findings.question: Within a stop, may a choice card go back to an earlier verse, like the 13:10 note about Sodom and Gomorrah asked after 13:12? Or must cards follow the passage strictly in verse order?
